title.value: M ASAKHA NEWS: N EWS T OPIC C LASSIFICATION FOR A FRICAN LANGUAGES
title.justification: The title of the paper is typically stated at the beginning and reflects the primary subject of the research, as seen in this document.
title.quote: M ASAKHA NEWS: N EWS T OPIC C LASSIFICATION FOR A FRICAN LANGUAGES

extractions.description: This paper presents the creation of the MasakhaNEWS dataset, a benchmark for news topic classification covering 16 African languages. The study evaluates and demonstrates the effectiveness of various machine learning and fine-tuning techniques on this dataset.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on NLP and data representation challenges for African languages, and there is no significant mention of climate change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: A BSTRACT African languages are severely under-represented in NLP research due to lack of datasets covering several NLP tasks.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on natural language processing tasks, particularly news topic classification for African languages. It does not directly address any climate change categories.
primary_category.quote: A BSTRACT African languages are severely under-represented in NLP research due to lack of datasets covering several NLP tasks.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no indirect connections to climate change topics; the paper strictly discusses NLP advancements and evaluations for African languages.
secondary_categories.quote: In this paper, we develop MasakhaNEWS — a new benchmark dataset for news topic classification covering 16 languages widely spoken in Africa.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any sub-categories under climate change priorities as defined. Its focus is solely on language model evaluation and dataset annotation.
primary_sub_category.quote: We provide an evaluation of baseline models by training classical machine learning models and fine-tuning several language models.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories related to climate change are addressed in the paper.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We provide an evaluation of baseline models by training classical machine learning models and fine-tuning several language models.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not address climate change or offer new insights related to it.
new_primary_category.quote: In this paper, we address two problems of lack of evaluation datasets, and lack of extensive evaluation of LLMs for African languages.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The research does not introduce new climate change sub-categories or applications.
